cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Pick a Priority
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to pick a priority. Your parents' gravy needs stirring and you need a lift to the station. Which job am I doing?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're looking for a shortcut. But a timer won't stir. Dinner or the station?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Dinner. I'll book a taxi. Just carry my suitcase downstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nearly learned it. My hands can't stir while they're carrying. Say which one you're choosing, and I'll do that one properly.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 taught prioritization frames the choice; A3 grades B2 shortcut but rejects a timer inability to stir; A5 grades B4 solution incomplete because the new favor uses the same hands.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 timer answer causes A3 physical limit; B4 taxi solves lift but case adds another job, causing A5 renewed choice.

relationship.evidence: B4 provides a real solution and a small residual request, giving A a specific next conflict.

heightening.evidence: A5 applies the same lesson at a smaller scale through B4 contribution, not an arbitrary added obstacle.

specificity.evidence: A1 gravy/lift and B4 suitcase establish practical exclusivity as A frames it.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 do-that-one-properly is a direct promise tied to B choosing.
